Sorry about the slight delay. Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: You may remember that at the beginning of each session I tend to ask you the same question, which is whether or not there is anything that you have already said that you wish to review in the light of the time that you've had to think about it.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: There's one thing that I would like to ask you arising out of something we've already discussed. Last Thursday, 18 May, you will remember I asked you a series of questions about the doctors that you believe have conspired against you to make things look worse --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- and you gave us four names.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Drs Brearey, Gibbs, [Dr B] and Jayaram.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: One thing I didn't hear you say, but which I saw from reading the transcript, was that there was some input from somebody else, but the name didn't appear on the transcript and I didn't hear it. Do you remember saying that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, that must be an error on my part. It's those four.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. Let me just remind you of the questions and answers and see if it jogs your memory because it may be important.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The question I asked was:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: Are you suggesting that there's some form of agreement between any of the medical staff who have given evidence in this case, some sort of agreement to get you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: In a consultant group, yes, I do believe that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: Who's in the conspiracy group then?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: Which individuals?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: I believe Ravi Jayaram, Stephen Brearey, [Dr B] and John Gibbs.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Question: So the Gang of Four; yes?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Answer: "Yes, possibly with input from --"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then the name, if you were about to give one, hasn't been recorded. So having had your memory jogged, were you about to give us another name?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We're going to move on now to the case of [Baby E]; all right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it your case that staffing levels contributed to the collapses or death of [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it your case that medical incompetence contributed to his collapse or death?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Possibly, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Whose medical incompetence?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The medical team that were on that night.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And who in particular are you suggesting was incompetent?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't think it's being incompetent, I just think collectively the doctors could have acted sooner to respond to his bleeding issue on reflection, seeing how much blood he had lost and what transfusion he was given or not given.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So reacted sooner?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes or treated the bleed.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, of course their reaction would be dependent on when you told them there was an issue, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you understand, don't you, that we, the prosecution, are suggesting that you didn't tell them as soon as [Baby E] did start to bleed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Because you will understand that it's the prosecution case that [Mother of Babies E & F] is telling the truth and that [Baby E] was bleeding at 21.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But you didn't tell anybody about that until at least an hour later, did you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't agree with that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When are you suggesting that something that wasn't done should have been done?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think once [Baby E] was profusely bleeding after 10 o'clock, maybe a blood transfusion or something could have been given sooner. I don't know if that would have made a difference to him.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. To whom do you attribute that mistake?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The medical team collectively. That's a medical decision.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So Dr Harkness?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And the other doctors. It was [Dr C], I believe, who was the consultant.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Was there another doctor on that night?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Only from his evidence, Dr Wood.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, Dr Wood, the SHO.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And we'll come back to him soon. So one or a combination of those three medical practitioners?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's a medical decision, yes, to prescribe and give a blood transfusion, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: During the evidence relating to [Baby E], do you remember that your friend Belinda Williamson gave evidence?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And she was asked about the plumbing and the drains in the neonatal unit when she gave evidence on 16 November.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you remember those questions?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't remember specifically, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What have the plumbing and the drains got to do with the death of [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't think I have ever said that they have got something to do with the death of [Baby E]. I think it's an important factor to note that there were often plumbing issues within the unit.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What has that got to do with the death or the collapses of any of these children?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm not saying that it is, but I think it's a contributing factor if the unit is dirty and staff are unable to wash their hands properly or we used to have raw sewage coming out of the sinks, running onto the floor in the intensive care nursery, and I think potentially that's not a safe working environment.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I don't know what effect that might have on a baby.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Raw sewage coming out of the sinks in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When did you first say that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I talked about there being sewage coming from the -- to the police.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Will we find a Datix form with raw sewage coming out of the sink in nursery 1 on it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not from myself, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Or are you aware of anybody putting in a Datix form --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know, but we often had the plumbers in attending to the sink in nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you're saying that the waste water was attached to, what, the soil pipe?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, we used to get backflow from the theatre sinks and — in the CLS/labour ward theatre sinks we used to get sewage coming back through the sink, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But you never filled in a Datix form?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not personally, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No. You did fill in a Datix form relating to the death of [Baby E] though, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'd just like to have a look at that, please. It's tile 218. We'll click on it, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just so that we understand, under what circumstances do you, and I'm talking about from your personal perspective now, under what circumstances do you fill in one of these forms?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: A Datix is completed as standard procedure if there's any death on the unit and then it's there for any other issues that I myself might want to raise that needs looking into, so any concerns I might have or anything that's gone against policy, anything that I think needs escalating to be reviewed by senior staff.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You filled in this form, did you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't remember from memory, but I'm assuming this is.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't...
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: As we've said many times, it isn't a memory test. Does the person who fills the form in, in effect, digitally sign it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And I think we'll see that on -- let's go to page 2, if we could, please, about a third of the way down. That's it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So we see incident reporter there, don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, so I filled in the form.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. And is there some way of knowing when this form was filled in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think at the very top of the form, I think there's a date and time if I'm correct. I'm not...
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. If Mr Murphy would oblige, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So there it was submitted on the 4th at 05.53.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that's you opening it; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's the time the form is submitted, so that's when it was filed and saved.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So this is an electronic process; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And do you have to put in your personal PIN number or something to access the blank form?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just as we scroll down it, would you tell us which bits you filled in? So the ID and the name and the reference, are they --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, that's automatically generated by the computer.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Even the name?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry? Yes, because it's part of the Meditech system.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So, what, you log into [Baby E]'s individual case, is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And this list of data that we see there self-populates?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: From memory, I think so, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. So we go to "location", which is the second section. Is that self-populated as well?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's something I would fill in. It's a drop-down box that you have to select from.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The coding section, next.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's me -- well, not the bottom two but the first four lines.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So "Clinical incident, neonatal unit". It says "pick list". Is that where you're hitting a drop-down menu?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The sub-category we see. We see this has got nothing to do with the result of staffing levels.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Which is your selection?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Risk grading. Is that what you put in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I'm not sure about that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It says "no harm caused", doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Which certainly doesn't make sense in the context of what we see in the next section. So "Details".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Incident date" selected by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The time of the incident, selected by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The fact that it's:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "An unexpected death following a GI bleed full resus unsuccessful."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then you have inserted the time of death; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Actions taken" and "Report to NRLS", is that done by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, the last input I have there is the "action taken".
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Those bottom two rows, they're not entered by me, I'm not sure what they stand for.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I think RIDDOR is something to do with the Health and Safety at Work Act, but we don't need to worry about that in the context of this case.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we scroll down, please. The next section, is that completed by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. The duty of candour, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then the incident investigation:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Please use this field to document all updates in relation to this investigation."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That has somebody else's name against it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that anything to do with you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So patient details, plainly you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I'm not sure if they are automatically generated or if I've put those in, but yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The next section, please, "Incident reporter", you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then we have, "Linked claims", "Linked records".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Nothing to do with you because that's opened, we see, on 2 August 2017.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And that's got somebody else's name as the handler, that's not myself.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. Can we go down to the next bit, please, and we then have something to do with other documents, but I would just like to scroll down, please. And keep going.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: SBAR, is this anything to do with you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. This is what's been completed at the review meetings by the staff that were listed above.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then continuing down, please, there's quite a long history of what happened to [Baby E] and when.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Nothing to do with you; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then can we keep going, please? And again, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: All this, nothing to do with you; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then the "SI panel meeting". Again, nothing to do with you? That's a meeting that happened in August 2015.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "SI tracker," again nothing to do with you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we continue? Any of this on the final page, anything to do with you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we can continue. Can you just identify anything else that is anything to do with you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: These are all just blanks, aren't they?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: They are, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we keep going.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's not me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's not me, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No, okay. So does it come to this, therefore, that so far as your input is concerned, it's simply in effect reporting the death, so what is at the bottom of the very first page?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, so it's standard practice if a baby dies that we select that on a pick list and submit a Datix, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I want to just deal with [Baby E]'s course of treatment and presentation before he came under your care on that night shift of 3 August.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we can start with tile 13, please. You cared for [Baby E] on the night shift of the 1st into 2 August, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That says [Baby F].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, I know, but I think you --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say from memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right, okay. Certainly you were designated nurse for [Baby F] on the 1st and indeed on the subsequent night anyway?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember sending a text on 2 August to one of your friends, saying, "Too Q word"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Too [quiet]"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not from memory, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we go to the [Baby F] sequence, please, to tile 26. I must have the wrong reference here. Well, we'll come back to it in the context of [Baby F].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is "Too Q word", is that a sort of thing that you would send in a text?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, possibly, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And what does it mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Q is -- we use -- the Q word is quiet.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so by "Too Q word", what did you mean by that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That the unit is quiet at that point.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It's tile 26 in the [Baby E], sorry. It's my note, I've written the wrong name. If we go to that in the [Baby E] sequence, please, it's tile 26:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Yeah, it's fine. Bit too Q word really."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you not like it when it was quiet?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, that's not what I'm saying. It's just sometimes it gets very quiet and we don't have many babies and you find you can be sitting around a lot and obviously we're there to help babies, so...
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you don't like it when there's nothing to do?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, there's always something to do, I didn't say there's nothing to do, but sometimes the shifts -- yes, sometimes they can be long nights if you haven't got as many babies on the unit, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So does it come to this then, that you enjoyed it when it was busy?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I enjoyed being busy, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So rather than being a negative, being busy, so far as you are concerned being busy was a positive?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I enjoyed being busy when it was managed, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We've just seen that on this particular shift -- so this is Sunday the 2nd into Monday, 3 August -- you were [Baby F]'s designated nurse --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- not [Baby E]'s.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't believe so, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we go to tile 30, please, on [Baby E]'s sequence? Can we just click on the -- go down to the bottom of the sheet, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's your handwriting, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there any reason that you were telling the doctors that they had made a mistake on the calculations when you were not the designated nurse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, because two nurses would have had to have verified that that prescription was wrong. So myself and another nurse would have had to have checked that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The other nurse on this shift was Mel Taylor, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall that from memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, that's what the evidence --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- shows. Why wasn't it -- Mel is senior to you, isn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She is.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why was she not speaking to the doctors given she was senior and this was her baby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It doesn't go on seniority. Two of you are responsible for signing a medication, therefore it's up to either of you to escalate any problems.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Had you fallen out with Mel by this stage --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- because she wouldn't speak to you about [Baby A]'s death in the aftermath of his death?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I hadn't fallen out with anyone, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is this an example, what we can see here, of the fact, of what Eirian Powell told us, that you were always prepared to call out other people's mistakes at the time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And that you were not afraid to confront the medical staff if you thought they had got it wrong?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you very confident in your abilities?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In my clinical competencies?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you think that you were a cut above some of the other nurses, including Mel?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Go to tile 61, please -- sorry, it's my fault, if we could go back to the previous part of this tile, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is Melanie Taylor's note; do you see that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You see where she records:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Mum and dad visiting at start of shift. Mum has been 2x with expressed breast milk overnight."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's what [Mother of Babies E & F] was doing, wasn't it, throughout this period? She was providing her own milk for her boys.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember her telling the jury when she gave evidence that at the time she felt it was the only thing that she could do for them?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And do you remember her always being very punctual in the provision of milk?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall that now. A lot of parents on the unit expressed, so I can't recall specifically what her expressing habits were.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we go to tile 104 next, please. This is [Nurse B]'s notes from towards the end of the day shift, which immediately precedes the night shift on which you were [Baby E]'s designated nurse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This shows very good progress, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And of course, this was day 6 of life for [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And he was doing very well, wasn't he?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: He is requiring insulin, so I wouldn't say he was very well, but yes, he is making progress with his feeds, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: There was no suggestion, was there, prior to you coming on duty at 7.30 or 8 pm on this day that he had any gastrointestinal problems?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, that's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And this was day 6 of life so far as he was concerned?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY
